synthesis.description: Arthur Andersen auditors send requests for their periodic testing (monthly gas testing, quarter-end P&L top sheets, MTM mini-book valuations, deal tickets and confirmations, index choices). Darron Giron receives them, forwards each to the desk or person who holds the support, collects what comes back and passes it to the auditors, chasing when replies lag. He also keeps a matrix of all requests made in a quarter and redirects requests for other desks, such as West desk work to Pat Ryder.
steps: Auditors send a request listing deals, books or figures they want support for.
The coordinator forwards the request to the trader, desk or risk contact who holds the data.
The contact pulls deal tickets, confirmations, valuations or P&L top sheets.
The coordinator chases contacts whose replies are late or asks who else can help.
Support is passed to the auditors, with explanations of differences where needed.
Open and closed requests are tracked in a request matrix for the quarter.
synthesis.approach: Keep a shared request log, built from the quarterly matrix, that records each auditor item, the desk owner, the date sent and the date answered, and flags overdue items for follow-up. Standard extracts of deal tickets, confirmations and P&L top sheets by deal number would cut the manual lookup each desk does.
synthesis.rationale: The work already revolves around a request matrix and repeated chasing; a structured tracker with owner by desk and status removes the guesswork over who holds the data and makes overdue items visible without manual status emails.
